hints: Remember how to read a skeletal formula, where every corner and end of a line is a carbon with enough hydrogens to make four bonds.
Count the carbons first (12 vertices in the three rings) and the two nitrogens, then work out hydrogens on the outer rings only.
Once you have the molecular formula, divide all subscripts by their highest common factor to get the simplest whole number ratio.
walkthrough:
**Read the skeletal formula**

Each vertex where lines meet is a carbon atom. Hydrogens are not drawn, but each carbon must have four bonds in total.

Rule: $\text{number of H on C} = 4 - (\text{number of bonds shown to C})$

**Count carbons and nitrogens**

There are two outer 6-membered rings, each with 6 carbons. The middle ring shares 4 of those carbons, so total C = 6 + 6 = 12. The two labelled atoms in the middle ring are N, so N = 2.

**Count hydrogens**

The 4 carbons at the ring junctions are bonded to 3 other atoms (C or N) already, so they have 0 H. The other 8 carbons on the outside edges are bonded to only 2 other atoms, so each has 1 H. That gives H = 8.

Molecular formula:
$$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{8}\text{N}_{2}$$

**Simplify to empirical formula**

Empirical means simplest whole number ratio. Divide all subscripts by 2:
$$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{8}\text{N}_{2} \rightarrow \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{4}\text{N}$$

options.A: This is the simplest ratio of $C_{12}H_{8}N_{2}$ divided by 2. It correctly shows 6 carbons, 4 hydrogens and 1 nitrogen in the lowest whole numbers.
options.B: This overcounts hydrogen. It assumes each outer carbon has more H than it does, forgetting that aromatic carbons in skeletal structures have only one H when two ring bonds are shown.
options.C: This is the molecular formula $C_{12}H_{8}N_{2}$, not the empirical formula. A common trap is to stop after counting atoms and forget to simplify to the lowest ratio.
options.D: This both fails to simplify and overcounts hydrogen. It counts 12 H as if every carbon had one H, but the four junction carbons bonded to N have no hydrogens at all.
